description.narrative: This project pics up the thread from the project Research Capacity and Cooperation Myanmar (RECCOM) MMR 17/0037, which was ran from 2018 to 2021. The new project is adapted to the dramatic events that took place since the inception of the previous project, mainly the military coup in Myanmar and the Covid pandemic. The current project supports Myanmar researchers and students through skills training, mentoring, and joint analytical/research/communications activities. The objective is to build analytical capacity in Myanmar society, including the growing Myanmar diaspora. The project also seeks to support peacebuilding and democratisation efforts and prepare Myanmar researchers in exile and within the country to contribute to rebuilding the country's political system and state. The project is thematically broad and open-ended, but special attention is paid to the challenge of handling climate impacts in the context of a divided society with a weak and fragmented state. It connects Myanmar researchers across ethnic boundaries in Myanmar and with a network of researchers in the ASEAN region and internationally. It also aims to contribute to more informed debate on critical Myanmar domestic and international issues. NUPI will establish a two-level network consisting of junior and senior Myanmar researchers inside and outside Myanmar. NUPI will engage with individuals and, where possible, Myanmar organisations that can contribute to the project's objectives. The project directly addresses SDG4 (Quality Education), SDG5 (Gender Equality) and contributes to SDG13 (Climate Action). The project puts particular emphasis on the promotion of women, and it is expected that half or more of all partners and beneficiaries will be women. Some of the work carried out under the project will also be on gender issues (details to be finalized in cooperation with partners).
